FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A37
The alcohol limit is 0.08% for drivers 21 and older but 0.02% for drivers under 21, so the younger limit is the stricter one. [A37]
Why it matters: group_hint impairment-limits; prereq_hint sec02-F18; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec02-F21, sec02-R02.
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A37
The THC limit is more than 5 nanograms per milliliter of blood for drivers 21 and older but anything above 0 for drivers under 21, which is a zero-tolerance rule. [A37]
Why it matters: group_hint impairment-limits; prereq_hint sec02-F18; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec02-F22, sec02-R01.
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A37
A test refusal suspension runs 90 to 730 days or until age 21, whichever is longer, which is a different range from the conviction suspension. [A37]
Why it matters: group_hint impairment-penalties; prereq_hint sec02-F20; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec02-F23, sec02-R04.
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A38
A DUI conviction suspension runs 90 days to 4 years, so it starts at the same floor as the refusal suspension but has a different ceiling. [A38]
Why it matters: group_hint impairment-penalties; prereq_hint sec02-F26; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec02-R03, sec02-F26.
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A37
Driving under the influence and being in physical control of a parked vehicle are both covered by the DUI law, under two separate sections, RCW 46.61.502 and RCW 46.61.503. [A37]
Why it matters: group_hint impairment-law; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec02-F18, sec02-F19.
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A32
Passing the knowledge exam opens a two-year window for the skills exam, and the skills exam can never be taken first. [A32]
Why it matters: group_hint exam-timing; prereq_hint sec02-F02; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec02-F03.
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A35
You may renew up to one year before expiration, but if the license has been expired 8 or more years you must retake both exams. [A35]
Why it matters: group_hint license-upkeep; prereq_hint sec02-F11; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec02-F11, sec02-F12.
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A39
An address change is done in License Express within 10 days, while a name change requires a visit to a driver licensing office. [A39]
Why it matters: group_hint license-upkeep; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 1; confusable_with sec02-F30.
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A39
Opened alcohol or cannabis may ride only in the trunk or truck bed, so no storage compartment within the driver's reach qualifies. [A39]
Why it matters: group_hint open-container; prereq_hint sec02-F28; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec02-F29.
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A36
A minor's alcohol, drug or firearm offense can delay the license until 17, which is different from the under-21 impairment limits that apply while driving. [A36]
Why it matters: group_hint losing-privileges; prereq_hint sec02-F13; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec02-F16, sec02-R01.
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0036]
